title: Fix cmd/guard fuzz-runner flake: worker start/finish failures misclassified as crashes
objective: Make the cmd/guard fuzz check deterministic under resource pressure: a Go fuzz worker that fails to start, communicate, or terminate must not be classified as a target crash, while genuine crashes and timeouts must still be reported.
nonGoals: no change to the bounded fuzz budget or fuzztime default
no suppression of genuine crash or timeout findings
nextAction: merge FJ-060 into main and re-verify the combined state
notes: Opened 2026-10-01 by PM from the FJ-041 cleaner reproduction. The classifier treats any '--- FAIL: <Target>' line as a crash, which includes Go's own worker start/communication/termination failures under load, and fuzzOutput.truncated is never consulted.

Reproduction: bash -c 'ulimit -n 64; go test ./cmd/guard -run TestRunFuzzPass -count=1 -v' -> 'guard.fuzz.crash p/fuzz_p_test.go 5 fuzz target FuzzSafe failed'. 32 load-only invocations did not trigger it, so it is environment-triggered rather than constant.
Impact: a spurious guard.fuzz.failed row makes ./scripts/verify-candidate exit non-zero for an unrelated candidate, which blocks any ticket coincidentally verified under the same pressure.

PM reproduction and evidence 2026-10-02: bash -c 'ulimit -n 64; go test ./cmd/guard -run TestRunFuzzPass -count=1 -v' -> findings=[{guard.fuzz.crash p/fuzz_p_test.go 5 fuzz target FuzzSafe failed}]. The underlying Go output for a minimal fuzz package under the same limit is: '--- FAIL: FuzzSafe (0.01s)' then '    fork/exec /var/folders/.../fz.test: too many open files' then 'FAIL'/'exit status 1'. So runOneFuzz's '--- FAIL: <Name>' branch declares a crash for a worker that never started. Genuine crashes are already caught by the primary written-crash-input branch (Go writes testdata/fuzz/<Name>/<id> for panics and t.Fail inside f.Fuzz).

PM ruling 2026-10-02 (owner of the coder's A/B question): option (a) - keep TestRunFuzzPass strict and follow the specifier. The defect was the FABRICATED guard.fuzz.crash finding, not the exit code; under fd pressure the tool genuinely cannot host a fuzz campaign, so an operational error is correct and fail-closed is preserved because the guard still exits non-zero (2 -> guard.tool.failed -> verify-candidate fails). My task-prompt wording '(must pass now)' was wrong and is superseded: the corrected success criterion is that the ulimit reproduction produces no crash finding, produces an operational error, and the guard exits non-zero. Rejected weakening TestRunFuzzPass (it would silently tolerate an unconstrained-environment tool error, the very tolerance that let this flake reach main) and rejected an RLIMIT_NOFILE shim (new build-tagged files outside allowedFiles, and it would mask the environment limit). Also noted: the coder correctly kept inputFingerprint = cleaner output and outputFingerprint = post-stage digest per design 6.1/7 rather than following the PM's incorrect instruction to set both equal.
